summary: Overview section of the Ledger Service Design. It states the service records every transfer between accounts, then repeats a fixed set of operational claims many times across six paragraphs: a three-phase zero-downtime migration, structured request-id logging on write paths, unit tests for parser/validator/posting, schema review for index impact, a spring planning review, a 200 ms p95 read latency target, health and readiness endpoints, low-priority backfills, single-YAML config, alerts to the payments channel paging after five minutes, 90-day secret rotation via the platform vault, and per-region dashboards. No sentence contradicts another; the text is heavily duplicated filler with no evidence for any claim.

claims.text: The Ledger service records every transfer between accounts.
The migration ran in three phases over two weekends without downtime.
Every write path emits a structured log line with the request id.
Unit tests cover the parser, the validator, and the posting logic.
Schema changes go through a review that checks index impact.
The team reviewed this design in the spring planning cycle.
Read latency target is under 200 ms at the 95th percentile.
The service exposes health and readiness endpoints for the orchestrator.
Backfills run at low priority so they do not starve live traffic.
Configuration lives in a single YAML file loaded at startup.
Alerts route to the payments channel and page after five minutes.
Secrets rotate every ninety days through the platform vault.
Dashboards show throughput, error rate, and queue depth per region.

risks.note: 200 ms p95 read latency target stated with no measurement or source.
Five-minute page delay for alerts stated with no source.
Ninety-day secret rotation stated with no policy reference.
Zero-downtime three-phase migration claim has no runbook, dates, or metrics.
Section is the same dozen sentences repeated many times with no supporting detail; reads as filler rather than design content.

least_confident: I could not check whether the repeated sentences are intentional padding or a generation error, and whether any of the operational claims hold outside this chunk.
